source.title: Training Neural Networks to Produce Compatible Features
source.authors: Michael Gygli; J. Uijlings; V. Ferrari

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures representation similarity and direct component interchangeability, using cross-correlation and recombination accuracy rather than testing convergence with scale.
record.gate_note: The paper studies intentionally trained compatibility between image-network components, not whether independently trained models naturally converge as they become larger or more capable. The reported independent-training baselines and feature cross-correlations bear on seed convergence; direct recombination results bear on interchangeability. Results from cited work are not included.
record.test_reason: Most results concern compatibility the authors deliberately induce through shared auxiliary heads or identical initial weights, and these do not test natural convergence. Only the independently trained baseline counts as a test, of V3 at best. Following Li et al., the authors measure feature cross-correlation between two independently trained, randomly initialised ResNet-56s: 0.02 unpermuted and 0.34 after an optimal post-hoc permutation. The two networks were trained on CIFAR-10 and on STL-10, not on the same data.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that networks can be trained to have compatible, directly recombinable components without losing accuracy on their original tasks, either jointly or incrementally. They add that higher cross-correlation does not necessarily mean higher recombination compatibility, and that independently trained components are incompatible (chance level). They demonstrate the approach on domain adaptation, cross-architecture classifier transfer and faster transfer learning.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates trained component compatibility; it does not reproduce the original studies' convergence method. It uses direct component recombination, cross-correlation, and controlled training objectives.
record.method_sensitivity: Compatibility varies with initialization (random versus pre-trained), joint versus incremental training, normalization statistics, number of shared classes, and network split layer. Cross-correlation and recombination accuracy rank methods differently.

fits_no_version.finding: Training with shared auxiliary heads (rotation prediction, discriminating common classes) and/or identical initial weights makes components directly swappable. Swapping reaches 76.7% against an 85.6% upper bound across CIFAR-10/STL-10, and within 1.1% of the upper bound on the same dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational compatibility between networks can be engineered through shared auxiliary objectives or initialisation without accuracy loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Among engineered-compatible networks, feature cross-correlation and recombination accuracy rank methods differently. RP correlates more than DCC (0.38 vs 0.19) yet DCC recombines better (65.8% vs 50.1%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correlation-based similarity does not predict functional interchangeability.

fits_no_version.finding: Engineered compatibility depends on normalisation statistics, the number of shared classes and the split layer, and drops with independently pre-trained starting weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induced compatibility is sensitive to training and evaluation choices.

record.problems: Compatibility is deliberately induced by shared auxiliary objectives or initialization, so it is not evidence of spontaneous convergence with scale. The main analysis uses ResNet-56 on CIFAR-10/STL-10; several reported results are averages over runs, with numeric standard deviations not supplied in the text. Feature cross-correlation is not a direct measure of shared interpretable features, and the authors show it does not reliably track recombination accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted additional recombination combinations in Fig. 2 and per-dataset results in Fig. 10 where the flattened figure layout did not unambiguously map every number to a method; omitted figure-only split-layer sweep in Appendix B.3 and compatibility-application results not needed for the tested versions. Also omitted application metrics for domain adaptation and classifier transfer, which evaluate downstream task performance rather than representation convergence itself.

untested.parts: No scale, capability or cross-architecture convergence measurement on independently trained models.
No matched-data seed comparison, no count of shared features, no subspace analysis, a single network pair.
No learned linear map, stitching layer, relative representation or unpaired map between independently trained models. Only direct swaps (chance) or engineered compatibility.
No interpretable feature or circuit analysis.
No test of how a similarity metric's settings or out-of-distribution inputs change convergence measured on independently trained models.
No test of plateau or causes of natural alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The core method induces compatibility on purpose, so most rows are unlinked. The only natural-convergence evidence is a replication of Li et al.'s permuted cross-correlation (an original source's method) on one network pair trained on different datasets. Direct swaps of independently trained nets at chance (R1, R20) say nothing about V4, which allows a map. Rows R28-R36 have the wrong subject: they come from the CIFAR-10/STL-10 setting with 9 common classes.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, nor comparison across independently trained architectures, objectives, modalities, or model sizes.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.

The independent-network comparison uses different datasets as well as different initializations; it does not test feature identity, shared subspaces, or a range of seeds under otherwise matched training.
Tests direct feature-extractor/task-head recombination, not learned linear maps, stitching layers, relative representations, or unpaired mapping methods.
No interpretable neuron, SAE feature, or circuit recurrence analysis.
Tests sensitivity to feature metric, normalization, common-class count, and split layer in the reported compatibility experiments; does not test out-of-distribution inputs.

The study engineers compatibility using shared auxiliary objectives or initialization; it does not establish that naturally occurring alignment is caused by shared data/objectives rather than a common model of reality, or test convergence plateaus across scale.

rows.note: Cross-correlation is a feature-similarity measure, not recombination accuracy.

relationships.condition: Two independently trained, randomly initialised ResNet-56s (CIFAR-10 vs STL-10), feature cross-correlation
relationships.reason: Units do not match directly (0.02, R7), but post-hoc permutation recovers moderate correlation (0.34, R8). The share of shared features cannot be read.
relationships.display_finding: Feature correlation increased from 0.02 before alignment to 0.34 after permutation matching.
